{{Short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Peter Schneider 2009.jpg|thumb|Schneider at [[Oberwolfach]], 2009]]
'''Peter Bernd Schneider''' (born 9 January 1953 in [[Karlsruhe]]) is a German mathematician, specializing in the ''p''-adic aspects of algebraic number theory,<ref>{{cite web|title=Leopoldina Neugewählte Mitglieder 2016, Leopoldina|location=Halle (Saale)|year=2017|page=42|url=http://www.leopoldina.org/uploads/tx_leopublication/Neugew%C3%A4hlte_Mitglieder_2016.pdf}}</ref> arithmetic algebraic geometry, and representation theory.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae Prof. Dr. Peter Schneider|website=Leopoldina Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Schneider_Peter_D_2016.pdf}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Peter Schneider studied mathematics in Karlsruhe and Erlangen. After his ''[[Diplom]]'' in 1977 from the [[University of Erlangen-Nuremberg]],<ref name=CV/> he was an assistant from 1977 to 1983 at the [[University of Regensburg]]. There he received in 1980 his PhD with advisor [[Jürgen Neukirch]] and dissertation ''Die Galoiscohomologie <math>p</math>-adischer Darstellungen über Zahlkörpern'' (The [[Galois cohomology]] of <math>p</math>-adic representations of [[number field]]s).<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=26732|name=Peter Schneider}}</ref> Schneider [[Habilitation|habilitated]] in 1982 at the University of Regensburg. He was a postdoc at Harvard University for the academic year 1983–1984 and a [[Academic ranks in Germany|C2-professor]] at [[Heidelberg University]] for the academic year 1984–1985. He was a [[Academic ranks in Germany|C4-professor]] from 1985 to 1994 at the [[University of Cologne]] and is since 1994 a C-4 professor at the [[University of Münster]].<ref name=CV/>

His research includes [[Iwasawa theory]], special values of [[L-function|<math>L</math>-functions]]. and [[p-adic number | <math>p</math>-adic]] [[Representation Theory|representations]] (in the latter subject he has collaborated extensively with Jeremy Teitelbaum).

In 1992 Schneider, together with [[Christopher Deninger]], [[Michael Rapoport]] and [[Thomas Zink]], received the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] for their work in using arithmetic-algebraic geometry to solve [[Diophantine equation | Diophantine equations]]. In 2006 he was an invited speaker with talk '' Continuous representation theory of p-adic Lie groups'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Madrid. In 2016 he was elected a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Peter Schneider|website=Leopoldina Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitglieder/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/8195/}}</ref> and the [[Academia Europaea]].
